newsitem.title: RUSSIA: IFC sees Russia shares in composite index Nov 1.
newsitem.headline: IFC sees Russia shares in composite index Nov 1.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation (IFC) will probably include Russian shares in its "composite investible index" on November 1, the IFC's head market analyst for central and eastern Europe said.
"Russia will be close to 2.7 to 2.8 percent of the composite index," Constantinos Grigoriadis of the IFC's emerging markets group said by telephone from Washington.

Many emerging markets funds use the IFC investible index to track the performance of emerging markets in areas where it is practically possible to invest. In some areas shares are tightly held and difficult or virtually impossible to obtain.
Other IFC indexes, so-called global indexes, track market performance with fewer restrictions linked to liquidity.
"The latest estimate we have is that $7-8 billion is tracking the IFC investable index," Grigoriadis said.
Some market sources had expected the IFC to add Russian shares to its investable composite this month.
"It definitely will not be by May," Grigoriadis said. "Most likely it will be November 1."

The IFC, the private-sector affiliate of the World Bank, focuses on equity and other investments in emerging markets. Its investable indexes track the free float of shares which can be bought readily in these markets.
Russia has been included in a number of IFC indexes preparatory to inclusion in the composite investable index.
Fifteen leading Russian shares were included in a separate Russia investible index in February and previously Russian shares were included in non-investable stand-alone and composite indexes.
Grigoriadis said that the investible Russian market capitalisation, representing the value of free float of shares in the investible-index companies, was about $22 billion.
Shares on the non-investible, so-called global index must represent 65-75 percent of the total and traded value of the market and are adjusted for cross- and government-holdings.
Shares with more than $50 million market capitalisation and $20 million traded per year are included in investable indexes, Grigoriadis said.
